Subject: Reliability SLO follow-up & competitive comparison

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What I heard on the call:
- Your primary concern is reliability and predictable behavior under sustained load and during regional failover.
- You want a side-by-side test vs your hyperscaler baseline (throughput, error profile, failover latency).
- Specific asks: uptime/SLA numbers, rate-limit behavior (burst vs sustained), 429 handling and Retry-After semantics, and how we degrade under pressure.

What I’m proposing:
1) Sharing a short SLO/SLA comparison doc (attached: redwood-slo-comparison.pdf).
2) A focused test plan to validate: steady-state throughput, burst behavior, cross-region failover, and error-budget burn characteristics.
3) A 2–3 day technical test window where we can temporarily raise limits and whitelist test IPs.

Attachments: redwood-slo-comparison.pdf (high-level SLA / behavior comparison).

Can you confirm:
- The target test regions (you mentioned us-east1 and us-west1 on the call)?
- A preferred test week (we’re proposing Mar 16–18 for a kickoff)?

Next steps from our side: I’ll work with Marissa and Ben to outline the test scenarios and expected pass/fail criteria, and we’ll send a short test-plan workbook and the exact limit increase request.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.ai>

Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire@cloudcorp.com>

Jordan —

Appreciate the follow-up and the PDF. Quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) SLA / uptime expectations: can you confirm numerical SLAs for the hosted product vs dedicated? Our security team expects both the contractual SLA and the "typical" operational numbers (e.g., block of time to failover).
2) Rate limits / bursts: what's the default per-org RPS and the max burst we can request for short tests? How does Redwood surface 429s (Retry-After header? exponential backoff recommended?).
3) Failover behavior: if you lose a region, do requests fail fast or route to another region? What is typical failover latency under load?

We want to run a 3-day comparison vs our hyperscaler baseline. Proposed regions: us-east1 and us-west1. If we can get a detailed test plan and a temporary limit increase, we’ll set up our load harness.

Also linking our internal test/infra checklist here for context: https://internal.acme.ai/infra-tests/reliability-checklist (internal link).

If you can provide the SLA numbers and a short runbook for handling 429s and error budgets, we’ll confirm the test window.

Thanks —
Sanjay
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme AI
sanjay.patel@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability SLO follow-up & competitive comparison (internal)

Jordan / Ben —

Drafted suggested answers and a test plan outline you can send to Sanjay. Keep it concise and operational. Quick notes you can paste into the reply: 

SLA / uptime (short):
- Hosted API: standard operational uptime ~99.9% (annual downtime ~8.76 hours).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): contractual SLA 99.99% (annual downtime ~0.876 hours) available on dedicated plans.
- We provide rollback & multi-region failover policies; for hosted customers we offer automated cross-region fallback for critical routes with expected failover windows under load of ~30–90s depending on connection in-flight state.

Rate limits / 429 behavior:
- Default: token-bucket shaped throttling; org-default is 200 RPS for API throughput.
- Burst: we can support short bursts to 500 RPS for hosted accounts (subject to capacity) and larger bursts for Dedicated. For the test we can temporarily raise limits to the requested values for a 72-hour window.
- 429s include a Retry-After header; recommend linear backoff and then exponential after repeated failures. Our SDKs surface Retry-After and will auto-backoff on application-level calls.

Error budget framing:
- For 99.9% SLA: error budget ~= 8.76 hours/year. For 99.99%: ~= 0.876 hours/year. Be explicit about how we measure (5xx & 429s that affect user-facing throughput).

Proposed test plan (short):
1) Steady-state throughput: sustain target QPS for 30 minutes (verify p50/p95/p99 latency and 5xx rates).
2) Burst test: 5-minute bursts at 2–3x steady-state (measure queuing, 429s, token-bucket refill behavior).
3) Failover test: simulate region outage (or route blackhole) and measure time to route and error spike; target < 90s for customer-visible recovery.
4) Error injection: run a short test that induces 5xx in a subset of requests to observe graceful degradation in consumer endpoints.

Attachments I’ll add: short test plan (redwood-test-plan.md) and the workbook Jordan will share with the customer.

Suggested message line to Sanjay: "We can support your 3-day comparative run; attached is a short test plan and a workbook. We can also temporarily raise your limits for the test and will provide a test account with IP whitelisting. Our hosted product operates at ~99.9% operational uptime; Dedicated offers a 99.99% SLA — we’ll include both numbers and the test pass criteria in the workbook."

LMK if you want me to draft the customer-facing workbook (I can export an xlsx).

—
Marissa
Director, Solutions & Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>

Sanjay —

Thanks for the quick questions. Per Marissa’s notes (copied below), here’s a concise package and proposed next steps: 

1) SLA snapshot (summary):
   - Hosted API: operational uptime ~99.9% (annual downtime ~8.76 hours).
   - Dedicated: contractual 99.99% SLA (annual downtime ~0.876 hours).

2) Rate limits & 429s:
   - Default org limit: 200 RPS. Bursts up to 500 RPS for short windows; we can bump this for a 72-hour test. 429 responses include a Retry-After header — we recommend linear then exponential backoff.

3) Failover behavior: automated cross-region fallback for critical routes; customer-visible recovery typically within 30–90s depending on in-flight requests.

4) Proposed test window & plan: kickoff Mar 16 (flexible). Attached: redwood-test-plan-20260310.xlsx (workbook with scenarios and pass/fail criteria). We’ll also provide a short run-of-show.

Next actions from Acme to enable the test:
- Confirm test regions: us-east1 and us-west1 (you already indicated these).
- Provide list of test IPs to whitelist and desired uplift in RPS during the test (we’ll request a temporary raise).
- Share your load harness endpoints and any authentication requirements we should pre-configure.

We’ve logged this in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345 (DEAL-ACME-2026-03). I’ll follow up after you confirm IPs to schedule a short tech kickoff.

Attachments: redwood-test-plan-20260310.xlsx

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a short tech call if you want to finalize scenarios.

—
Jordan Blake
